author: m. a. zimmerman
title: Rep. Adam Smith urges end to shutdown and warns of health care cost increases
text:
Rep. Adam Smith, who represents Washington’s 9th district in the U.S. Congress, used his social media platform on October 15, 2025, to address the ongoing government shutdown and its effects on health care and federal services.
In a post made at 13:03 UTC, Smith wrote, “Two weeks of suspended services. Two weeks with critical health care at risk. Two weeks of Republican vacation. It’s time for them to come back to work for the American people and end this shut down.”
Later that day, at 14:34 UTC, he added, “As long as Republicans need Democratic votes to pass government funding, they need to come to the table to negotiate with us.”
At 18:13 UTC, Smith addressed the financial impact on Americans if health care tax credits expire. He stated, “A 60-year-old couple earning $82,000 will see premiums rise by $14,875 the GOP allows health care tax credits to expire. That’s a 237% increase. My Democratic colleagues and I remain ready to work today to reopen the government with a bipartisan agreement that protects health.”
Smith has served in Congress since 1997 after succeeding Randy Tate. He previously held office in the Washington State Senate from 1991 to 1997. Born in Washington, D.C., in 1965, Smith is currently 57 years old and resides in Bellevue. He holds a BA from Fordham University and a JD from the University of Washington.
